description:
Italians Who Fed Omaha is a podcast from La Casa Pizzeria dedicated to preserving the stories of the Italian and Sicilian families who helped shape Omaha’s food culture.

 

Hosted by Tony Vacanti Jr., a fourth-generation pizzaiolo and owner-operator of La Casa Pizzeria, the series explores the people, restaurants, bakeries, recipes and traditions that helped define how Omaha eats. These are stories of immigration and family, Little 

Italy and neighborhood restaurants, hard work and entrepreneurship, and generations of Omahans gathering around the table.

 

La Casa has been part of Omaha’s restaurant community since 1953. Through Italians Who Fed Omaha, La Casa is helping document and preserve the history of the families and businesses that built Omaha’s Italian food scene, while sharing the stories behind some of the city’s most recognizable food traditions.

 

Season One features conversations with the families and people behind La Sole Mio, Caniglia’s, Orsi’s Italian Bakery, Cascio’s Steakhouse, Rotella’s Italian Bakery and La Casa Pizzeria. Together, their stories trace generations of Omaha food history, from the bakeries and Italian steakhouses of Little Italy to family restaurants and the distinctive pizza traditions that became uniquely Omaha.

 

Italians Who Fed Omaha is for anyone who loves Omaha history, Italian food, local restaurants, family businesses and the people who helped make Omaha taste like home.

description: Have you ever wondered if there’s actually a best time to take your multivitamin? For most people, taking a multivitamin with a meal is a simple and convenient choice. So, choose a convenient mealtime, follow the recommended serving instructions, and make your daily multivitamin part of a healthy routine.”

title: Collapse
author: gaming huge
description:
Collapse tells the true stories of the world's great structural failures and the engineering that grew up in their wreckage. Each episode, host Nirob takes one collapse — a railway bridge that dropped a train into a Scottish estuary on a winter night, a dam that emptied a reservoir onto a valley of sleeping towns, a hotel walkway that fell on a dance, a suspension bridge that twisted itself apart in a moderate wind — and rebuilds it: the structure and the confidence that built it, the flaw hidden inside it, the moment of failure as it actually happened, the toll and the inquiry, and the change in the codes and the science that came out of the ruins.

From the Tay Bridge and Johnstown to Tacoma Narrows and Ronan Point, from the Hyatt Regency and Banqiao to the Sampoong department store and the Morandi Bridge, Collapse is about the strange fact that we trust our lives every day to structures whose designers have never met us — and about the small mistakes, the ignored warnings and the honest miscalculations that have brought them down. Meticulously researched, clear about the engineering, and honest about where the fault really lay. Clean and suitable for all ages. A new collapse every week

Who are the separatists? What do they actually want?

Separation Anxiety is a five‑part investigative series from award‑winning Alberta journalists Danielle Paradis and Tim Querengesser that aims to find out.


Join them as they follow organizers into church boardrooms and hot‑dog picnics to examine the influences, ideas and grievances fuelling Alberta’s modern separatist movement.

That's what Lived Mastery is for.

It's about coming back to that edge again and again until the coming back becomes who you are.
Every episode delivers:
A real story – the version entrepreneurs and leaders don't usually tell, the empty bank account, the loan to make payroll, the darkest-before-the-dawn moment.

Be strong.
Don’t complain.

description:
The Human Experiment: Psychology, Behavior & the Science of Being Human

Why do we trust some people instantly but distrust others without knowing why? Why do we follow crowds, fear things that rarely happen, remember certain moments for years, and make decisions we later regret?

Welcome to The Human Experiment, a documentary-style podcast exploring the psychology, behavior, neuroscience, and hidden forces that shape the way humans think and act.

Hosted by Ethan Reed, each episode investigates a fascinating question about human behavior from cognitive biases and social influence to memory, emotions, decision-making, attraction, fear, habits, persuasion, conformity, and the strange ways our brains interpret the world around us.

We explore famous psychological experiments, groundbreaking discoveries, surprising behavioral studies, real-world stories, and everyday situations that reveal something deeper about being human.

✔️ Why do people obey authority?
✔️ Why does rejection hurt so much?
✔️ Why do we procrastinate even when we know the consequences?
✔️ Why are first impressions so powerful?
✔️ Why do intelligent people sometimes believe obviously false ideas?

The Human Experiment turns complex psychology and behavioral science into compelling stories that are easy to understand and difficult to forget.

No complicated academic lectures. No endless jargon.

Just fascinating questions, evidence-based explanations, unexpected discoveries, and practical insights into the human mind.

Whether you're interested in psychology, neuroscience, human behavior, science, relationships, decision-making, or simply understanding yourself and other people better, The Human Experiment invites you to look at everyday human behavior from a completely different perspective.

Because every day, without realizing it, we're all part of the experiment.

title: BIBLE MEMORY | Mnemonics, Scripture, Bible Study, Neuroscience, Trust in God, Memorization
author: Keaghan Otto - Memory Coach
description:
Have you ever flipped open your Bible to a ”new” verse only to realize you’ve actually highlighted that exact passage and made notes on it already? Or you just know that you read something the other day that would be so encouraging for your current anxiety or fear, but you just can’t seem to find that specific verse again?
GUUUURL same!
I’m so grateful you’re here! This podcast is all about practically writing the Living Word on our hearts; so it’s there when you need it, not just somewhere in a notebook you can’t find. And no, it’s not just saying a verse 100 times. It’s quick, it’s simple, and honestly? It’s kind of fun. Stick with me!
Hey, I’m Keaghan. A Jesus-loving wife and mama who still struggles with fear, anxiety, and the constant ”am I doing enough” … all while racing a ticking clock and a never-ending to-do list. I tried living life the world’s way, and honestly, unsubscribe!
I hustled, tried harder, and did more. I got the management job and the degree like they said. It almost ruined me. In my first year of varsity, studying a BSc, the panic attacks led to a family intervention. 
That’s when I started learning HOW to actually learn. Life shifted dramatically,  I spent nearly as much time studying my own brain as I did studying for my degree. I got that degree with a distinction, had a baby in my final year, and worked full time through it. It took years after that to connect those study methods to how I read and learn my Bible. But I got there! Praising Jesus for His goodness and patience with me along the way!
Now I’m still on this journey, just like you. As I keep walking imperfectly with the Lord, He keeps showing me how wonderful our brains actually are and my joy keeps increasing. Learning is so much more possible than we often think. 
If you’re ready to read and memorize your Bible so you have an arsenal at your disposal for when life be ”life’ing” with quick, easy, simple methods that actually stick, this podcast is for you.
So prepare your heart.

Katie Robertson by Margaret Winslow.  
Katie Robertson is a tale of a girl who takes on factory work as a means of assisting her widowed mother. The novel introduces the reader to a variety of topics of the day in the late 19th century in the USA for young Christian people and the temptations in the wider world: the problems associated with alcohol and the temperance movement, the dignity in work, the freedoms afforded to immigrants. Welcome back to the Oh Mel Podcast.

It’s 2026, and after stepping away from the microphone, I’m back.

So much has happened since I last recorded in May 2025. Life has changed. I’ve changed. I’ve experienced things, learnt things, questioned things, grieved, grown and gained a whole new perspective.

So this feels like the right time for a new chapter.

Same Mel. New chapter.

This is a fresh season of the Oh Mel Podcast
A place for honest conversations about life, faith, trauma, therapy, grief, abuse, childhood and adolescent mental health, relationships, upbringing, generational and intergenerational trauma, and the things we don’t always feel comfortable talking about.

Whether you believe in God, you’re questioning your faith, or you don’t believe at all, you’re welcome here.

I’m not coming back as a completely different person. I’m still Mel. But I’m not the same Mel I was when you last heard me.

And I think that’s worth talking about.

So, welcome back to Oh Mel.

New season. Fresh eyes. New perspective. New conversations.

Let’s talk.

📧 I’d love to hear from you:
ohmelpodcast@gmail.com

Send me your questions, thoughts, feedback or your own experiences. Let’s have a conversation around the podcast and please feel free to share it with someone who might need to hear it.

title: Iron Road
author: Sami Indonesian
description:
Iron Road tells the true stories of the world's great railway disasters and the making of railway safety. Each episode, host Nirob takes one disaster — a bridge that failed under a train in a winter storm, a signalman who forgot a train was coming, a runaway train on a mountain grade, a high-speed train that derailed in the night — and rebuilds it: the railway and the technology of its age, the rules and the procedures that failed or were ignored, the accident as it happened, and the change in the signalling, the brakes, the training and the safety culture that came out of the wreck.

From the first great bridge disaster at Norwalk to the fall of the Ashtabula bridge, from Armagh and Quintinshill to Harrow and Clapham, from Eschede and Ladbroke Grove to Amagasaki, Wenzhou, Santiago and Lac-Mégantic, Iron Road is the story of how the most dangerous form of transport ever invented became, by the measures of the modern age, one of the safest. Meticulously researched, clear about the engineering, and honest about the difference between the record and the legend. Clean and suitable for all ages. A new disaster every week

Fast forward: I've completed 16 full marathons, 100+ half marathons and more shorter distances than I can cound -- including 7 World Major Marathons (New York, Chicago, Boston, Berlin, London, Tokyo and Sydney). My second Boston Marathon and each of the international marathos happeded after I turned 60. I'm still running, still race directing for non-profit organizations that need someone who understand what it takes to get people to the starting line and cheer them on at the finish line. 
Do you find yourself asking:
-Is it too late or am I to old to start running or walking?
-How do I get started and stay motivated when everything hurts a little more than it used to?
-What does it actually look like to keep moving - physically and in life - through the midlife chapter?
This podcast is for you if:
-You're navigating midlife and want to start or keep moving.
-You want real talk instead of empty motivation.
-You want to be at the starting line instead of on the sidelines
-You want proof that adventure, momentum, and reinvention are very possible - no matter where you are starting from!
Midlife Miles is built around three things I believe are deeply connected:
1. Movement & Training:
   Practical topics - running, walking, and exploring incluidng how to actually get going and keep going. 
2. Life in Motion: 
    The mindset, resilience and reinvention that comes with our stage of life. 
3. Adventure & Travel: 
    Moving forward should sometimes mean a passport stamp, not just a training log. 
    Running, walking, & exploring through midlife in whatever form that means for you.

title: Change Your Life with Dr Amen Kaur: Build Self Love, Self Worth, Self Confidence and the Courage to Achieve Your Goals
author: Dr. Amen Kaur
description:
You have something of immense value to give. Something happened, and now you feel unsure of yourself.  You doubt yourself and your self confidence has gone.
Maybe it was redundancy, or a divorce, or a new manager who chipped away at your value until you stopped trusting yourself. Maybe you were quietly managed out. Maybe nothing dramatic happened at all and you have just been asking, is this it? Either way you want more, you cannot go back to what it was, and you cannot make yourself move forward the way you used to.
That is not a strategy problem.
Most advice gives you one half of the answer. One half is all structure, the plans and the tactics, with no inner foundation to hold it up, so what is really driving you is fear and proving yourself. The other half is all inner work, sitting with your feelings and never taking an action. Both leave you feeling stuck, lost, overwhelmed and burned out.
This show is about doing both, in the right order. Self love first, because when you do not have it you stop believing you are worth what you want. Then self worth, so you can trust what you know. Then self value, so you can express it and actually experience it. Then the systems and structures that make it compound. Build your value on the inside. Achieve your goals on the outside.
I'm Dr. Amen Kaur. I have spent over twenty years helping people achieve their goals, including as a partner in an FTSE 250 business. I am a researcher at heart, so I look for the root cause rather than treating the symptom. What I bring you here is research, science and spirituality, because the convergence of all three brings us to a core truth.
Each week we look at answering the questions you are actually asking. How do I start my life over? What do I actually want? How do I find my purpose after losing my job? How do I deal with a career change when I have no idea what I want next? How do I recover after a breakup or a divorce? How do I start a business when I don't know what I want and my confidence has gone? Is it too late to start over? Should I start a business, or go back to a job after self-employment? Is a career coach worth it?
And underneath those, the questions that decide the answer. Why do I keep self sabotaging. Why do I procrastinate. Why do I people please and over give and prove my worth. Why does my confidence go when someone devalues me. Why do I keep attracting toxic relationships and toxic bosses. Why do I feel undervalued when I know I'm good at what I do. How do I stop feeling anxious about a decision I already know I want to make.
We work through self love, self worth and self value, and the practical, tactical things they let you do. Getting the promotion. Building the business. Finding career clarity when you are feeling stuck mid career. Setting boundaries without guilt. Regulating your nervous system so you can think straight. Building the systems and structures that compound, at work and in a business, so the results keep coming without you burning yourself out to get them.
You cannot be told your value. You have to experience it.
If you are feeling lost, feeling stuck, or wondering what to do next, start with any episode and see what lands.

Because growing your business should be... easy. brzy.

description:

title: The Defining Move | Leadership and CEO Evolution for Scaling Businesses
author: Richard Medcalf | CEO Strategic Leadership & CEO Transformation Expert
description:
As a founder or CEO scaling your business, what do you do when the next big leap isn't happening fast enough?
Most CEOs respond by making time for strategy, improving strategic execution, hiring stronger leaders, or working even harder.
Eventually you hit a business plateau, because the real constraint isn't strategy or systems. It’s Leadership Leverage – your ability to make bolder decisions, break the CEO bottleneck, build executive team ownership, and create a scaling culture.
And leverage grows when a CEO makes a defining move – an irreversible decision that changes who they must become to lead the next version of the business.
That's what this show explores.
The Defining Move is a podcast about CEO leadership for scaling businesses, and the CEO transformation that drives the next level of growth.
Unlike other CEO leadership shows, we don’t discuss past successes. We watch what happens when elite leaders face high-stakes challenges.
In every episode, Richard Medcalf hands one of the world's most accomplished leaders a fictional defining move, already made, that changes the trajectory of their business.
You’ll learn from how they think and how they lead when the stakes rise. And you’ll discover the hidden sources of leadership leverage that take them to their next level, and will take you to yours.
Richard Medcalf, founder of Xquadrant, CEO coach, and author of Making TIME For Strategy and The 10X Reckoning, has advised founders and CEOs of scaling businesses for over 20 years – from disruptive scale-ups to billion-dollar corporations – on CEO leadership, CEO transformation, and executive team development.
The show helps founders and CEOs strengthen their CEO leadership, accelerate CEO evolution, and build businesses that can scale without becoming dependent on the founder.
Episodes explore founder & CEO leadership, CEO transformation, CEO accountability, executive team ownership, vision execution, strategic execution, strategic leadership, strategic decision making, leadership leverage, founder bottlenecks, CEO bottlenecks, scaling culture, CEO evolution, business plateaus, and the defining decisions behind extraordinary companies.
You'll also discover Richard's practical frameworks for CEO transformation: Leadership Leverage, Leadership Constraints, The Defining Move, The 10X Reckoning, and other ideas that help founders and CEOs evolve to lead organisations that scale faster than their own personal capacity.
Questions we explore include:
How do you break the founder/CEO bottleneck?  
What creates leadership leverage?  
How do you build executive team ownership and accountability?  
Why do leadership teams struggle with strategic execution?  
How do you create a scaling culture?  
How do you build an accountability culture?  
How do you scale without becoming the centre of every important decision?  
What separates CEOs who hit a business plateau from CEOs who create extraordinary businesses?  
What does CEO evolution entail?  
When is it time to make a defining move?  
How does CEO transformation drive business growth?
If you're building a scaling business and believe your next breakthrough depends on your own CEO evolution, not simply better strategic decision making, you'll feel at home here.
Popular Episode Topics Include: CEO Leadership, CEO Transformation, CEO Accountability, Executive Team Ownership, Founder Bottleneck, CEO Operating System, Vision Execution, Vision Execution Gap, Strategic Leadership, Strategic Decision Making, Scaling Culture, Accountability Culture, Leadership Leverage, Organisational Leverage, Business Plateau, Scaling a Business Without Burnout, and CEO Evolution.
Previously published as The Impact Multiplier CEO, this podcast continues to explore CEO leadership for scaling businesses through a new format centred on defining decisions and CEO transformation.

title: The Ruler's Back: The Making of The Blueprint by Jay-Z
author: Breaking Atoms
description:
By 2001, Jay-Z was no longer chasing the throne. He was sitting on it. But with his biggest album yet, he was about to prove why he belonged there.



The Ruler’s Back: The Making of The Blueprint is the definitive audio documentary exploring the creation of Jay-Z’s landmark 2001 album, The Blueprint. Through deep research, rare stories, and exclusive interviews with key figures involved in the album’s creation, including Young Guru, Bink and Just Blaze, the podcast goes behind the music to uncover the people, places, ideas and pivotal moments that shaped one of the most influential albums in Rap history.



Originally produced and released by Breaking Atoms in 2021 to celebrate the 20th anniversary of The Blueprint, this acclaimed podcast returns for the album’s 25th anniversary with newly remastered audio. From the soul samples and stripped-back production to Jay-Z’s defining performances and the intense circumstances surrounding its release, hear the story of how The Blueprint came together - and why its influence can still be felt a quarter of a century later.

Hosted on Acast. See acast.com/privacy for more information.
